name: ערך מוחלט וארגומנט של חזקת מספר מרוכב (באנגלית)

functions.name: cxTX
functions.body: first(args(e))

functions.name: cxsq
functions.body: block([f,m:1,s:1], if n=1 then [1,1] else (f:ifactors(n), for p in f do (m:m*p[1]^floor(p[2]/2), s:s*p[1]^mod(p[2],2)), [m,s]))

functions.name: cxrat
functions.body: if integerp(y) then string(y) else sconcat(if y<0 then "-" else "", "\\frac{", abs(num(y)), "}{", denom(y), "}")

functions.name: cxtx
functions.body: if float(x)<0 then sconcat("-",tex1(-x)) else tex1(x)

functions.name: cxnn
functions.body: block([q,ms,c,g,ps,y], y:ratsimp(radcan(x)), if ratnump(y) then cxrat(y) else (q:ratsimp(radcan(x^2)), if not ratnump(q) or q<0 then cxtx(x) else (g:if float(x)<0 then "-" else "", ms:cxsq(num(q)*denom(q)), c:ms[1]/denom(q), ps:sconcat(if num(c)=1 then "" else string(num(c)), "\\sqrt{", ms[2], "}"), if denom(c)=1 then sconcat(g,ps) else sconcat(g,"\\frac{",ps,"}{",denom(c),"}"))))

functions.name: cxpa
functions.body: if float(x)<0 then sconcat("\\left(",cxnn(x),"\\right)") else cxnn(x)

functions.name: cxi
functions.body: block([s], b:if float(b)<0 then -b else b, if b=1 then "\\mathrm{i}" else (s:cxnn(b), sconcat(s, if integerp(ratsimp(radcan(b))) then "" else "\\,", "\\mathrm{i}")))

functions.name: cxs
functions.body: block([a,b], z:rectform(z), a:realpart(z), b:imagpart(z), if b=0 then cxnn(a) elseif a=0 then sconcat(if float(b)<0 then "-" else "", cxi(b)) else sconcat(cxnn(a), if float(b)<0 then "-" else "+", cxi(b)))

functions.name: cxps
functions.body: block([a,b], z:rectform(z), a:realpart(z), b:imagpart(z), if (a=0 or b=0) and float(a+b)>=0 then cxs(z) else sconcat("\\left(",cxs(z),"\\right)"))

functions.name: cxas
functions.body: block([c,p,ps,g], c:ratsimp(x/%pi), if not ratnump(c) then cxtx(x) elseif c=0 then "0" else (g:if c<0 then "-" else "", p:abs(num(c)), ps:sconcat(if p=1 then "" else p, "\\pi"), if denom(c)=1 then sconcat(g,ps) else sconcat(g,"\\frac{",ps,"}{",denom(c),"}")))

functions.name: cx
functions.body: TX(cxs(z))

functions.name: cxp
functions.body: TX(cxps(z))

functions.name: cxn
functions.body: TX(cxnn(x))

functions.name: cxa
functions.body: TX(cxas(x))

functions.name: cxP
functions.body: TX(cxpa(x))

functions.name: cxrt
functions.body: block([s:cxnn(sqrt(N)), t:sconcat("\\sqrt{",cxrat(N),"}")], TX(if s=t then t else sconcat(t,"=",s)))

functions.name: cxpq
functions.body: if float(x)<0 or not integerp(ratsimp(x)) then sconcat("\\left(",cxnn(x),"\\right)") else cxnn(x)

functions.name: cxQ
functions.body: TX(cxpq(x))

functions.name: cxugly
functions.body: is(ssearch("^{\\frac",tex1(x))#false)

functions.name: cxquad
functions.body: block([x:float(realpart(rectform(z))), y:float(imagpart(rectform(z)))], if abs(x)<1e-12 then (if y>0 then 5 else 6) elseif abs(y)<1e-12 then (if x>0 then 7 else 8) elseif x>0 then (if y>0 then 1 else 4) else (if y>0 then 2 else 3))

functions.name: cxmod
functions.body: TX(sconcat("\\sqrt{",cxpq(realpart(rectform(z))),"^2+",cxpq(imagpart(rectform(z))),"^2}"))

questiontext:
Given that \(z\) is the complex number

\[ {{CT:0}}, \]

evaluate the modulus and the principal value of the argument of \({{CT:1}}\). Give your answers in the correct order i.e. \([r,\theta]\)

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Write \(z\) in polar form (modulus \(r_1\) and argument \(\theta_1\)), apply De Moivre's theorem, and bring the argument into the principal range \((-\pi,\pi]\).
Step 1 — The modulus of z
Write \(z=x+yi\) with \(x={{CT:2}}[[if test="{{CT:19}}"]]={{CT:3}}[[/if]]\) and \(y={{CT:4}}[[if test="{{CT:20}}"]]={{CT:5}}[[/if]]\). Then

\[ r_1=|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=\sqrt{\left({{CT:2}}\right)^2+\left({{CT:4}}\right)^2}=\sqrt{{{CT:6}}}={{CT:7}} \]

Step 2 — The argument of z
The ratio \(\tan\theta_1=\frac{y}{x}={{CT:8}}\) alone does not determine \(\theta_1\); the quadrant is needed too. The argument depends on the quadrant of the point \(({{CT:3}},{{CT:5}})\) in the complex plane. [[if test="{{CT:21}}"]]Let \(\alpha\) be the acute angle between the segment from the origin to the point \(({{CT:3}},{{CT:5}})\) and the \(x\)-axis:

\[ \alpha=\arctan\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|=\arctan {{CT:9}}={{CT:10}} \]

[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:22}}"]]The real part is positive and the imaginary part is positive, so the point is in the first quadrant and \(\theta_1=\alpha\). [[/if]][[if test="{{CT:23}}"]]The real part is negative and the imaginary part is positive, so the point is in the second quadrant and \(\theta_1=\pi-\alpha\). [[/if]][[if test="{{CT:24}}"]]The real part is negative and the imaginary part is negative, so the point is in the third quadrant and \(\theta_1=-(\pi-\alpha)\). [[/if]][[if test="{{CT:25}}"]]The real part is positive and the imaginary part is negative, so the point is in the fourth quadrant and \(\theta_1=-\alpha\). [[/if]][[if test="{{CT:26}}"]]The real part is 0 and the imaginary part is positive, so the point lies on the positive imaginary axis. [[/if]][[if test="{{CT:27}}"]]The real part is 0 and the imaginary part is negative, so the point lies on the negative imaginary axis. [[/if]]Hence

\[ \theta_1={{CT:11}} \]

Step 3 — De Moivre's theorem
For \(z=r_1(\cos\theta_1+i\sin\theta_1)\) and \(n={{CT:12}}\), \({{CT:1}}=r_1^{n}\left(\cos n\theta_1+i\sin n\theta_1\right)\). So the modulus is

\[ r=r_1^{{{CT:12}}}={{CT:7}}^{{{CT:12}}}={{CT:13}} \]

and an argument is

\[ {{CT:12}}\theta_1={{CT:12}}\cdot\left({{CT:11}}\right)={{CT:14}} \]

Step 4 — The principal argument
The principal value of the argument lies in \((-\pi,\pi]\). Adding or subtracting multiples of \(2\pi\) does not change the direction, so [[if test="{{CT:28}}"]]we subtract \(2\pi\cdot {{CT:15}}\):

\[ \theta={{CT:14}}-2\pi\cdot {{CT:15}}={{CT:16}} \]

[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]we add \(2\pi\cdot {{CT:17}}\):

\[ \theta={{CT:14}}+2\pi\cdot {{CT:17}}={{CT:16}} \]

[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:30}}"]]the angle above is already the principal value:

\[ \theta={{CT:16}} \]

[[/if]]The answer, in the order \([r,\theta]\):

\[ \left[{{CT:18}},\ {{CT:16}}\right] \]
